title: Chaliapin’s boatmen, near and far
work: Song of the Volga Boatmen, arranged by Chaliapin and Keneman
question: How does Chaliapin build a whole drama from the boatmen’s repeated call?
intro: Men hauling barges along the Volga sang to coordinate each heave. Chaliapin and Fyodor Keneman made their work song into a piece for bass and orchestra. Chaliapin keeps returning to the same short call, swelling it into a shout and letting it dwindle.

recordings.label: Fyodor Chaliapin, George W. Byng
recordings.note: Made through an acoustic horn, with Byng conducting: Chaliapin’s first recording of the arrangement he helped create.

recordings.label: Fyodor Chaliapin, Albert Coates
recordings.note: The microphone remake, with Coates conducting, made five years after Chaliapin’s first version.

passages.label: The call grows stronger
passages.note: The bass gives the repeated call more force, building a long swell from the short phrases.

passages.label: The first shout subsides
passages.note: Chaliapin reaches the top of the swell, then softens the next phrases as the orchestra continues beneath him.

passages.label: The song swells again
passages.note: The repeated call gathers strength again. The bass sustains the rise across successive phrases.

passages.label: The boatmen recede
passages.note: The voice grows quieter, and the last calls fade into the orchestral accompaniment.
